note: Items Android MUST have although the iOS baseline has no counterpart. Not a platform difference (that is _whitelist.json) and not an unknown (that is _unrecognized.json): these are deliberate additions caused by a different data source or a different responsibility split. The extractor merges them into the page contract with an `androidOnly` object; the checker counts them as expected on Android, lists them in the report, and fails when `reason` does not answer the three questions, when `reviewBy` is past, or when the item no longer matches anything on the Android page (stale). Admission rules (spec/ui/v1/page-structure-rules.md): only items forced by a different platform or data source, never a product choice (that is a baseline §7 GAP); not when the baseline already offers an equivalent recovery/entry on the same page; and not when the item renders only behind a nullable callback the shipping PdshNavHost route never passes.

reasonShape.baselineLacks: why the iOS baseline does not need this item
reasonShape.androidNeeds: why Android cannot do without it
reasonShape.withoutIt: what breaks for the user if it is not there

reason.baselineLacks: the baseline scatters the matching grammar across an input placeholder and a validation sentence, so it has no syntax section
reason.androidNeeds: the Android page edits a host-owned list where an empty table means deny-all, so the `*.suffix` / port / scheme rules must be stated once, on the page

reason.baselineLacks: the baseline deletes a workspace from the drawer's `⋯` menu (SessionsPage.swift:447), not from this page
reason.androidNeeds: README §1 gives this page the add/remove duty, and the Android drawer has no workspace menu, so removal must live here

reason.baselineLacks: WorkspaceFoldersPage (NativeShell.swift:319) draws `management.workspaces` from the in-process `DSHManagementModel.shared` (`:320`, `:326`); its body has no failure state, so it has no retry to offer
reason.androidNeeds: the Android rows are host facts carried by a snapshot read across the process boundary: `WorkspaceFoldersScreenState.from` maps `snapshot.failure` to `FAILED` and deliberately keeps no rows, so the page must be able to re-read in place
reason.withoutIt: a failed read leaves only the failure line on an otherwise empty page; dismissing it does not restore the rows, so the user has to leave and re-enter the page to get a list back

reason.baselineLacks: the iOS page has no 引擎 group: it renders 状态 and 已运行 as one untitled row above 本次运行 (`runtimeRow("状态", statusValue)`, ChatPage.swift:4184), and `statusValue` is assembled at runtime from `model.displayStatus` plus the elapsed time, so the extractor's section model has no group to compare
reason.androidNeeds: the Android page folds its diagnostics by group, and the engine rows are that group: `RuntimeSectionView(ENGINE_SECTION_ID, 引擎, …)` owns the fold and the `runtime.engine.status`/`runtime.engine.uptime` row ids, while the contract's untitled-group criterion only proves that the 停止本地引擎 row exists somewhere below
reason.withoutIt: the status and uptime rows would sit above 本次运行 with no header and no fold id, so the user could not collapse them and the stop action would lose the group it belongs to

reason.baselineLacks: the iOS page shows no WebView row: WebKit ships with the OS, so `platform.webview-version-gate` records that iOS has no separately updatable core version and no boot-time feature probe to display
reason.androidNeeds: Android's WebView is a separately updated package that can be missing or disabled, so `platform.webview-version-gate` requires the provider, the version (telemetry only, never the gate) and the `WebViewFeature.isFeatureSupported` probe to be visible; this page is the only surface that shows them
reason.withoutIt: a device whose WebView lacks a required feature would degrade the page surface silently, with no on-device evidence of which feature is missing

reason.baselineLacks: the iOS page does not show the memory tier, budget or usage; `platform.budgettier-memory` keeps that read in `Sources/PhoneDSHController/Budgets.swift`, behind the budgets policy rather than on the runtime page
reason.androidNeeds: the Android host picks the tier once per boot from `ActivityManager.MemoryInfo` and enforces the budget, so the chosen tier and the measured usage are host facts the page must show; `overBudget` also raises a page note
reason.withoutIt: an over-budget session would surface only as a generic degradation with no numbers, and the tier chosen for this device could not be checked against what the host enforced

reason.baselineLacks: the iOS page exposes neither the thermal state nor battery, charging or battery-saver; `platform.thermal-battery` records that the signals drive the budget policy on both platforms, but iOS does not render them here
reason.androidNeeds: `PowerManager.getCurrentThermalStatus` plus the `BatteryManager` signals are the inputs of the conservative policy; Android's thermal granularity is coarser than iOS's, so the page prints the platform's own level and never treats an unread signal as normal
reason.withoutIt: a severe thermal level or an enabled battery saver would change background behaviour with no on-page explanation, so the user would read a deliberately conservative engine as a fault

reason.baselineLacks: iOS has no foreground service: `platform.fgs-turn-notification` records that background progress is presented by the system UI and BGContinuedProcessing, so the baseline page has no availability row to show
reason.androidNeeds: whether a foreground service can start is the Android signal that decides whether a background turn can outlive the foreground; the row also carries the host's own reason when it cannot start (this App declares no service), which is a measured fact rather than an assumption
reason.withoutIt: the difference between 'the turn stopped because the app went to the background' and 'this build can never keep running in the background' would be invisible to the user

reason.baselineLacks: iOS exposes the workspace to the system Files app (UIFileSharingEnabled + LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace in examples/probe-app/Config/PhoneDSHProbe-Info.plist), so files are imported there and FilesPage needs no import control
reason.androidNeeds: the Android workspace lives in app-private storage that no other app or system file manager can write, so the only way to bring a file in is the host's document picker (HostShell.kt passes onFilesImportRequest = onPickWorkspaceFile from MainActivity)
reason.withoutIt: an Android user has no way to put a document into the workspace for the agent to read
